resolutions.researcher_notes: Old current_ref carried a '?cf-view' query suffix that fails the verifier (200 but token-blocked); the same URL without the query string verifies OK and states the field/pipelines were 'brought on stream in December 2017' reaching full capacity in 2019 -- i.e. still operating, not a one-time event. Corroborated independently by S&P Global's energyconnects.com (Aug 2025, 'Egypt expands drilling at Zohr gas field as output recovery efforts continue') and Egypt Oil & Gas (zohr-field-hits-2-bcf-d... 2025), both confirming the field/pipeline system is actively producing as of 2025 -- i.e. operating, not shelved/idle. NS Energy Business and Offshore Technology are both GlobalData/Verdict-Media network sites sharing one underlying project database (same boilerplate text) -- treated as one origin, not two independent sources; the energyconnects.com piece is the genuinely independent second source. No contradiction found.

Both sources describe the Zohr-El Gamil line(s) as natural gas pipelines carrying gas from the field to the onshore treatment plant ('two 216km-long 30in-diameter gas pipelines'). NS Energy/Offshore Technology (GlobalData network, one origin) and araburban.org (independent origin) agree. No contradiction.

Wikipedia ('Zohr Field') and araburban.org both independently state production/first gas came on stream in December 2017 (araburban: 'began operations in December 2017 ... only 28 months after discovery'). NS Energy/Offshore Technology (same GlobalData origin) agree but are not counted as the second independent source. No contradiction on the year.

VALUE DISCREPANCY: every source found (NS Energy, Offshore Technology, araburban.org, Saipem project page) gives the Zohr-to-El Gamil subsea/onshore trunk as ~216 km (two 30in pipelines; a later phase cites 215-218km segments), not the sheet's recorded 210.00 km. Close (~3% off) and unambiguously the same physical pipeline/segment (same 30in diameter, same Shorouk-to-El Gamil route), so I am staging these as supporting refs for the row/segment identity, but the exact 210 km figure is not independently corroborated -- recommend Update review the LengthKnown value against 216 km. Tier set to medium for this reason despite two independent sources on the general pipeline description.
Both independent sources describe the pipeline(s) as carrying gas produced by the Zohr field to the El Gamil onshore treatment facility -- directly supports FuelSource = Zohr Field. No contradiction.

Start (Shorouk concession, Mediterranean Sea offshore, Egypt) and end (Al Gamil/El-Gamil, Port Said, Egypt) both directly and independently corroborated: NS Energy/Offshore Technology and araburban.org both name the Shorouk Block offshore field and the 'AL-Gameel'/El-Gamil onshore treatment facility in Port Said Governorate; Wikipedia independently places Zohr in the Shorouk Block ~190km north of Port Said. No contradiction.

CONTRADICTION FLAGGED, not resolved: could not find any independent source supporting the sheet's Owner1-4 split (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co 48%, Eni SpA 26%, Naturgy 13%, SEGAS 13%; sums to 100%). This does not match either real ownership structure I could verify for this asset family: (a) the Shorouk concession/Zohr field contractor's share is Eni 50% / Rosneft 30% / BP 10% / Mubadala Petroleum 10% (nsenergybusiness.com, offshore-technology.com, araburban.org, thenationalnews.com/mubadala.com on the 2017-18 stake sales) -- Naturgy and SEGAS are not parties to this concession at all; (b) the Damietta SEGAS LNG plant (a separate GEM entity, Al Gamil is NOT the same site as Damietta) is owned Eni 50% / EGAS 40% / EGPC 10% as of the 2020-21 restructuring (eni.com press releases; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SEGAS_LNG gives the pre-2020 structure as Union Fenosa Gas [Eni+Naturgy JV] 80% / EGAS 10% / EGPC 10%). Neither real structure produces 48/26/13/13, and 'SEGAS' itself is the LNG plant company, not a plausible co-owner of an upstream trunk pipeline -- this looks like the Owner fields for this pipeline record were populated from/confused with the separate Damietta SEGAS LNG Terminal entity's ownership rather than researched for this pipeline. Recommend a human review of the Owner1-4 values themselves before any ref is sought; no verifiable value = no ref to cite, so left UNRESOLVED with the contradiction on record rather than fabricating support.
